_comment: 1 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. This file walks one night at a fictional logistics yard through the four operational classes no standard covers: a missed patrol checkpoint, a late post arrival, and a trespass episode from report through response to disposition (events 3-6 share a correlation_uid). Here: the overnight tour's 22:00 run never registered checkpoint 4 — derived by schedule correlation, not observed by a device.

2 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. The relieving officer reaches the South Gatehouse 45 minutes after the scheduled 22:00 start: a Late Arrival with the signed variance in milliseconds, backed by a clock punch (derivation Direct). The post object carries its required post_type_id.

3 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. The gatehouse officer finds two people inside the fence line near the north dock and files an incident report: incident_type_common 'trespass' from the published vocabulary, the organization's own label alongside in incident_type_internal, verified by an on-site check.

4 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. The mobile unit rolls: Response Activity is one event per phase, each with its own time, and every phase event carries the unit's full four-timestamp timeline on response_resource so no consumer has to reassemble the interval.

5 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. Eight minutes later the same unit is on scene — the next phase of the same response, same correlation_uid, dispatch-to-on-scene interval readable straight off the resource timeline.

6 of 6 — SYNTHETIC example — invented site, times, and identifiers; no operational data. The label that makes the night's data worth keeping: a human triages the episode as genuine (cause Genuine, AVS Level 1, verified On Site Check, Responded Verified), fourteen minutes from report to triage. A signal with a disposition is a training example, an audit record, and a benchmark row.
